title: States Prepare for Possible Federal Intervention in Midterm Elections
description_short: States Prepare for Possible Federal Intervention in Midterm Elections
description_medium: HuffPost reported that state officials were preparing for possible federal action affecting the November 2026 midterms. The article recounted Trump’s calls to cancel the elections and his statement that he might declare an emergency to federalize election administration if Congress did not pass the SAVE America Act. It describes contingency planning, not a completed takeover.
description_long: In an August 2026 report, HuffPost described state officials preparing for the possibility that the Trump administration would challenge state control of the upcoming midterm elections. It reported that Donald Trump had suggested canceling the elections over alleged voter fraud and said he might declare a national emergency to federalize election administration if Congress did not pass the SAVE America Act. State officials told HuffPost they had identified possible avenues for federal intervention and were preparing to resist actions they considered unlawful. The article also recounted federal pressure on state election officials, including Justice Department letters to all 50 states warning of prosecution over noncitizen voting, canceled election-protection training, and removal of a protection manual. Legal experts discussed the division of authority between state election administration and congressional regulation. The report documents statements and preparations; it does not show that Trump declared an emergency, canceled the midterms, or took control of their administration. The title is therefore framed around preparation for possible intervention rather than completed election meddling.
notes: Focused read of the linked HuffPost report supports state officials’ preparations and Trump’s statements about canceling the midterms or federalizing administration if Congress did not pass the SAVE America Act. It describes possible action, not a completed takeover.

title: Trump Pardons Alex Adjmi on January 19, 2021
description_short: The DOJ clemency roster lists Alex Adjmi among Trump’s January 19, 2021 pardons.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s pardon roster lists Alex Adjmi among the pardons granted on January 19, 2021. It identifies two federal cases: a Connecticut money-laundering case and a New York conspiracy-to-commit-insurance-fraud case, with the sentences and penalties recorded in the table. The roster does not give Trump’s reason for granting the pardon.
description_long: The Justice Department’s roster of pardons granted during Donald Trump’s 2017–2021 term lists Alex Adjmi under January 19, 2021, and identifies two federal cases. For the District of Connecticut, it records a 48-month prison sentence, three years of supervised release conditioned on 600 hours of community service, and a $125,000 fine for money laundering. For the Eastern District of New York, it lists three years of supervised release, a $15,000 fine, and $4,500 restitution, as amended, for conspiracy to commit insurance fraud. The roster documents the recipient, the offenses, and the listed case penalties. It does not state why Trump selected Adjmi or provide the individual pardon instrument’s exact terms. This account reports the clemency action and case information in the federal listing; it does not infer corruption from the offenses or from the former category label, and it does not allege a political connection.
notes: Focused read of the linked DOJ pardon roster confirms Alex Adjmi’s January 19, 2021 entry and the two listed cases with sentence details. The roster does not provide a reason or recipient-specific pardon terms; neither is asserted here.

title: Trump Commutes Michael H. Ashley’s Sentence on January 19, 2021
description_short: Trump commuted Michael H. Ashley’s sentence on January 19, 2021.
description_medium: The Justice Department commutations roster lists Michael H. Ashley under January 19, 2021, for an Eastern District of New York bank-fraud case. It records a 36-month prison term, five years of supervised release, and $49,307,759.84 in restitution as the original sentence. The roster does not state the revised term or whether restitution and supervision changed.
description_long: The Justice Department’s commutations roster lists Michael H. Ashley under January 19, 2021, and identifies a 2019 bank-fraud case in the Eastern District of New York. The entry records an original sentence of 36 months’ imprisonment, five years of supervised release, and $49,307,759.84 in restitution. Those figures describe the sentence associated with the case before the commutation; the public table does not state the new term, remaining time, or whether any other conditions changed. It also gives no recipient-specific explanation for the clemency decision. The listing confirms a commutation but cannot show how much punishment was reduced or whether restitution and supervision remained in force. The signed commutation instrument or a court record is needed to describe those effects. No political connection or corrupt motive is inferred from the grant itself.
